Simulated motor claims with premiums

Source: R/reserving_data.R
simulated_motor_claims.Rd

The paid and incurred claims of a simulated motor portfolio, by accident year 2014 to 2025 and development year, with each accident year's earned premium: a table in the long form that as_triangle turns into triangles. Each year's loss ratio is around 68%, and its payments follow a development pattern with over-dispersed (gamma) noise; the incurred claims add case reserves that each year sets a little high or low. The script that made it is in the package's source, under data-raw.

Usage

simulated_motor_claims

Format

A data frame with 78 rows, one per accident and development year of the past, and 5 columns:

accident_year

the accident year, 2014 to 2025;

development_year

the development year, 1 for the accident year itself;

paid

the claims paid in the development year (incremental);

incurred

the change in the incurred claims (paid claims and case reserves) over the development year (incremental);

earned_premium

the accident year's earned premium, on each of its rows.

See also

as_triangle, bornhuetter_ferguson, cape_cod and munich_chain_ladder.

Examples

triangle <- as_triangle(simulated_motor_claims, "accident_year", "development_year", "paid",
                        cumulative = FALSE)
premium <- unique(simulated_motor_claims[c("accident_year", "earned_premium")])$earned_premium
cape_cod(triangle, premium)$total
#>              latest             premium          loss_ratio      prior_ultimate 
#>        6.929459e+07        1.204310e+08        6.971151e-01        8.395427e+07 
#>            ultimate                ibnr ultimate_loss_ratio 
#>        8.395427e+07        1.465967e+07        6.971151e-01
